newsitem.title: LEBANON: Labour leader says Hariri wants union destroyed.
newsitem.headline: Labour leader says Hariri wants union destroyed.

text.p: Lebanese leftist labour leader Elias Abou Rizk on Wednesday accused the government of Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri of trying to destroy the country's labour movement.

Speaking to reporters before flying to Geneva to attend an international labour conference, Abou Rizk vowed to carry on fighting for democracy and freedoms. On Saturday, he was released on bail after being detained on charges brought against him by a rival labour leader.
"Destroying the labour movement is a strategic goal for Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri's government to cover its failure in solving social and economic problems," Abou Rizk said.
"It seems that they knew from the beginning the results of their bad social and economic policies...so they planned to seize the labour unions by all means," he added.

He was arrested for eight days after General Labour Confederation (CGTL) elections in April produced two leaderships -- one headed by him and one by Ghneim al-Zoghbi, who was recognised by the government.

"We once again confirm our legal status as CGTL chief... Despite the arrest and despite the government's use of power against us, we will be tougher now in our struggle to defend freedom, democracy and the daily bread," he said.
Abou Rizk, 54, said that ever since last month's elections he has been receiving threats over the telephone from unknown parties.
"I have informed top officials about that, and that I am still receiving such such threats and that is why they sent me bodyguards," he said.
Abou Rizk, who was seeking a second four-year term as CGTL chief, harried Hariri during his first term with general strikes and demonstrations to demand better conditions for workers.
